elements.element: The licence extends to Customer’s affiliates without requiring written notice.
elements.evidence: The grant covers Client’s affiliates only “on written notice to TrueLink,” which imposes the fallback notice condition.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer’s behalf.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause grants rights only to Client and its notified affiliates; it contains no rights for contractors acting on Client’s behalf.
No perpetual protection is provided. Section 2 is subject to the one-year term, non-renewal and termination provisions. The existence of paid-up licences is not demonstrably excluded.
The clause does not state that any licence is irrevocable, and Section 13 expressly permits Section 2 to terminate. The existence of paid-up licences is not demonstrably excluded.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated only for a material breach.
elements.evidence: Section 13 permits non-renewal on 30 days’ notice and termination for any breach of Sections 8a–8c, without requiring materiality; it also references termination under Section 12.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated for breach only after that breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: Section 13(b) permits termination for violations or breach of Sections 8a–8c without an express cure opportunity, and other termination or non-renewal routes are not conditioned on an uncured breach.

elements.element: Customer may transfer the licence without consent to any successor, rather than only a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: The consent exception is limited to Client’s successor “in a merger or acquisition,” so it does not provide transferability to successors generally.

elements.element: The licence covers Customer’s affiliates upon written notice to the licensor.
elements.evidence: Section 2(a) grants the licence to Client and, “on written notice to TrueLink, its affiliates.”

elements.element: Customer may transfer the licence or Agreement without consent to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 15 waives the approval requirement for an assignment by Client “to a successor in a merger or acquisition.” Because the licence is a right under the Agreement, it transfers with that permitted assignment.

result.reason: The operative insertions fully implement both fallback requirements and do not add unrelated obligations or disturb the existing field of use, non-exclusive status, term or general assignment regime. They do not satisfy the preferred position because affiliate coverage is notice-conditioned, contractors are omitted, no perpetual or irrevocable paid-up protection is added, subscription termination remains broader than uncured material breach, and successor transferability is limited to merger or acquisition transactions.
